summary: James Ishmael Ford is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He earned a BA at Sonoma State University and an M.Div. and MA at the Pacific School of Religion, while also studying under Sojun Mel Weitsman, Jiyu-Kennett, and John Tarrant.

James Kenneth Powell II works in Buddhist studies. He studied at Northwestern University (BA), the University of Chicago (M.Div.), and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD, ending 1998), with teachers including Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Isshi Yamada, David Tracy, and David M. Knipe.

James L. Fitzgerald works in Indology and religious studies. After completing his PhD at the University of Chicago (1980) under Edwin Gerow and J. A. B. van Buitenen, he held posts at the University of Tennessee and Brown University.

James Legge was a sinology scholar educated at Aberdeen Grammar School, the University of Aberdeen (MA, circa 1831–1835), and Highbury College. He was appointed Professor at the University of Oxford in 1876.

James Luther Adams was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Minnesota, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University, where he later held a post from circa 1956 to 1968.

James Mackintosh was a scholar of history, archaeology, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Aberdeen and University of Edinburgh, and he founded the Asiatic Society of Mumbai, serving as its president from circa 1804 to 1811.

James Mallinson is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He earned a master's at SOAS and a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He held posts at SOAS and became Oxford's Boden Professor of Sanskrit in 2023.

James Mark Shields is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. In 2016, he was attested as Associate Professor at Bucknell University and an Overseas Collaborative Researcher at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies.
James Matthew Baskind is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his PhD at Yale University under the supervision of Stanley Weinstein (attested 2006).

James McHugh is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Cambridge, Oxford, and Harvard (PhD), studying under scholars including Lawrence McCrea, Anne E. Monius, and Parimal G. Patil. He held posts at Cornell and the University of Southern California.

James Miller is a scholar in sinology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Cambridge (MA, 1997) and Boston University (PhD, 2000), and was Professor of Chinese Studies and Religious Studies at Queen's University Belfast (attested 2014).
James Morison was an Indology scholar who studied under Georg Bühler. He served as Librarian at the Indian Institute, Oxford (attested 1917) and at the University of Oxford (attested 1920).

James Murdoch was a scholar of Japanology, history, and archaeology. Educated at the University of Aberdeen and under Theodor Benfey, he held academic posts in Japan at the University of Tokyo, Kanazawa University, and Kagoshima University.

James Prinsep was an Indology and history scholar who worked at the Kolkata and Benares Mints. He led The Asiatic Society (1832–1838), was a Fellow of the Royal Society, and founded the Journal of the Asiatic Society of Bengal.

James R. Ballantyne was an Indology, philosophy, and linguistics scholar educated at Edinburgh under James Michael and Francis Johnson. He served as master at the Scottish Naval and Military Academy, Principal at Benares Sanskrit College, and librarian at the India Office.

James Robson is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. Educated at UC Santa Barbara and Stanford (PhD, 2002), he held posts at Williams College, University of Michigan, Harvard University, and became director of the Harvard-Yenching Institute in 2024.

James Smith Reid was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Cambridge (circa 1865–1869). He subsequently held posts at Christ's College, Pembroke College, and Gonville and Caius College.

James Sutherland Cotton was a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He was educated at Winchester College and Trinity College, Oxford, and subsequently held posts at Queens' College, Cambridge, and Queen's College, Benares (1871–1874).

James Tod was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at the Royal Military Academy, Woolwich, and under Gyanchandra, he served with the East India Company and as Librarian of the Royal Asiatic Society (circa 1823–1835).
James W. Benson is an Indology and linguistics scholar. He held posts attested at Harvard University (1999), the University of Oxford (1999), and Wolfson College, Oxford (2001).
